declared.title: Satisfaction in choice as a function of the number of alternatives: When “goods satiate”
declared.foundIn: rapport contre-preuve reports/too-many-choices/counter-evidence.md (2026-11-22), DOI trouvé par ses requêtes ; titre relevé sur Crossref par la session : contrôle d'identité plus faible

population: participants choosing among sets of alternatives of different sizes (varying in colour or shape); sample and country not given in the abstract

findings.text: In an experiment, satisfaction from choosing first rose then fell as the number of alternatives grew (an inverted U, as the authors proposed)
Satisfaction peaked at a larger number of options when the options were easier to compare (differing in colour rather than in shape)

limits: each support sentence only says the proposition « is verified » or « validated »: no size, no sample in the abstract
published in the 2009 issue with two studies pooled by scheibehenne-2010-overload; possibly pooled too (not checked)
